data.narrative:
Skeleton Technologies is a Series E-stage frontier-tech company in the Climate & Energy sector that has raised €392M to date. The valuation universe consists of one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. The Climate & Energy sector contains nine same-sector peers total, though none meet the combined filters of stage alignment, valuation tier similarity, and sufficient sample size.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable to this analysis. While nine same-sector peers exist, the combination of stage specificity (Series E), valuation tier, and business model similarity yields insufficient datapoints—zero same-stage matches, two adjacent-stage matches, and zero similar-tier matches. A median calculation from fewer than three comparable observations would introduce unacceptable selection bias and misrepresent the comparability threshold. An unfiltered all-sector median would further obscure the idiosyncratic risk and capital intensity profiles specific to Climate & Energy infrastructure companies.

Without sufficient peer data meeting multiple triangulation criteria, a single-point valuation estimate cannot be defensibly derived from this dataset. The analysis would require either: broadened stage/tier filters with explicit risk adjustments; revenue or unit economics multiples if operational data were available; or expansion of the peer set through private transaction data. The key uncertainty is whether the two adjacent-stage comparables can anchor a range once adjusted for stage progression.
